title: Contravariant word evaluation descends through the simplex relations
statement: Use the presentation category of [lem-sc-module-cup-godement-simplex-presentation-faithful], with its full definition recalled here. Let $P$ have objects $[n]$ for $n\geq0$ and arrows finite composable words in generators $\delta_i:[n-1]\to[n]$ ($n\geq1$, $0\leq i\leq n$) and $\sigma_i:[n+1]\to[n]$ ($0\leq i\leq n$), modulo the category congruence generated by $\delta_j\circ\delta_i=\delta_i\circ\delta_{j-1}$ for $i<j$, $\sigma_j\circ\delta_i=\delta_i\circ\sigma_{j-1}$ for $i<j$, $\sigma_j\circ\delta_j=1=\sigma_j\circ\delta_{j+1}$, $\sigma_j\circ\delta_i=\delta_{i-1}\circ\sigma_j$ for $i>j+1$, and $\sigma_j\circ\sigma_i=\sigma_i\circ\sigma_{j+1}$ for $i\leq j$, with degree superscripts suppressed and only typed instances imposed. Let $\mathcal D$ be an ordinary category, with objects $U_n$ for $n\geq0$, arrows $d_i:U_n\to U_{n-1}$ for $n\geq1$, $0\leq i\leq n$, and $s_i:U_n\to U_{n+1}$ for $0\leq i\leq n$. Assume, whenever both composites are defined, $d_i\circ d_j=d_{j-1}\circ d_i$ for $i<j$, $d_i\circ s_j=s_{j-1}\circ d_i$ for $i<j$, $d_j\circ s_j=1=d_{j+1}\circ s_j$, $d_i\circ s_j=s_j\circ d_{i-1}$ for $i>j+1$, and $s_i\circ s_j=s_{j+1}\circ s_i$ for $i\leq j$. Contravariant word evaluation, sending $[n]$ to $U_n$, each $\delta_i$ to $d_i$ and each $\sigma_i$ to $s_i$, is constant on each congruence class of words. It therefore defines a functor $E:P^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal D$ with these object and generator values; for composable presentation arrows $p,q$, $E(q\circ p)=E(p)\circ E(q)$, and the empty word at $[n]$ has value $1_{U_n}$.

source.place: Tag 016B, lemma-characterize-simplicial-object (2), proof through Tag 0168, lemma-face-degeneracy-category (b),(c): evaluation on the presented category before passage to Delta.

proof.text: For a generator $a:[m]\to[n]$, put $v(\delta_i)=d_i$ and $v(\sigma_i)=s_i$, so $v(a):U_n\to U_m$. Define $V(\varnothing_{[n]})=1_{U_n}$ and, recursively on the number of letters, $V(a\circ w)=V(w)\circ v(a)$. Thus for $w:[m]\to[n]$ the value has type $U_n\to U_m$. In particular a one-letter word has value $v(a)$ by the identity law. This constructs evaluation on actual words before imposing any relations.

source.place: Tag 016B, lemma-characterize-simplicial-object (2), proof via Tag 0168, lemma-face-degeneracy-category: elementary expansion of evaluation on words modulo the relations.

proof.text: For composable words $p,q$, prove $V(q\circ p)=V(p)\circ V(q)$ by induction on the length of $q$. If $q$ is empty, both sides are $V(p)$ by the identity law. If $q=a\circ q'$, the recursive definition and induction hypothesis give $V(q\circ p)=V(q'\circ p)\circ v(a)=(V(p)\circ V(q'))\circ v(a)=V(p)\circ(V(q')\circ v(a))=V(p)\circ V(q)$. The last reassociation is the category associativity axiom.

source.place: Tag 016B, lemma-characterize-simplicial-object (2), proof via Tag 0168, lemma-face-degeneracy-category: elementary expansion of evaluation on words modulo the relations.

proof.text: The evaluations of the two sides of each defining relation are, in the order in the statement: $d_i\circ d_j$ and $d_{j-1}\circ d_i$; $d_i\circ s_j$ and $s_{j-1}\circ d_i$; $d_j\circ s_j$ and $1$; $d_{j+1}\circ s_j$ and $1$; $d_i\circ s_j$ and $s_j\circ d_{i-1}$; $s_i\circ s_j$ and $s_{j+1}\circ s_i$. These are equal by the six assumed identities, with exactly their stated index inequalities. The identity words here have the correct source degree because only typed instances of the presentation relations are imposed.

source.place: Tag 016B, lemma-characterize-simplicial-object (2), proof via Tag 0168, lemma-face-degeneracy-category: elementary expansion of evaluation on words modulo the relations.

proof.text: For parallel words define $w\mathrel R w'$ to mean $V(w)=V(w')$. Equality is reflexive, symmetric and transitive, so $R$ is an equivalence relation on each set of parallel words. If $w\mathrel R w'$ and $a,b$ are any words for which $b\circ w\circ a$ is defined, the concatenation formula of step 2 gives $V(b\circ w\circ a)=V(a)\circ V(w)\circ V(b)=V(a)\circ V(w')\circ V(b)=V(b\circ w'\circ a)$. Thus $R$ is stable under both composition contexts. By step 3 it contains the generating relations. The category congruence in the definition of $P$ is the least such equivalence relation stable under these contexts, so it is contained in $R$. This proves that evaluation is constant on every congruence class.

source.place: Tag 016B, lemma-characterize-simplicial-object (2), proof via Tag 0168, lemma-face-degeneracy-category: elementary expansion of evaluation on words modulo the relations.

proof.text: Set $E([n])=U_n$ and $E([w]^{\mathrm{op}})=V(w)$. Step 4 makes the arrow assignment independent of the representative. For $p:[m]\to[n]$ and $q:[n]\to[r]$, step 2 gives $E([q\circ p]^{\mathrm{op}})=V(p)\circ V(q)$, exactly the functor composition law on $P^{\mathrm{op}}$. The empty-word formula gives the identity law. Step 1 gives $E(\delta_i^{\mathrm{op}})=d_i$ and $E(\sigma_i^{\mathrm{op}})=s_i$. These verify every asserted object, generator, composition and identity value.

lean.statement: theorem simplexWordEvaluation_descent {D : Type u} [Category.{v} D] (U : ℕ → D) (d : ∀ n : ℕ, Fin (n + 2) → (U (n + 1) ⟶ U n)) (s : ∀ n : ℕ, Fin (n + 1) → (U n ⟶ U (n + 1))) (hdd : ∀ (n : ℕ) (i j : Fin (n + 2)), i ≤ j → d (n + 1) j.succ ≫ d n i = d (n + 1) i.castSucc ≫ d n j) (hds_lt : ∀ (n : ℕ) (i : Fin (n + 2)) (j : Fin (n + 1)), i ≤ j.castSucc → s (n + 1) j.succ ≫ d (n + 1) i.castSucc = d n i ≫ s n j) (hds_self : ∀ (n : ℕ) (j : Fin (n + 1)), s n j ≫ d n j.castSucc = 𝟙 (U n)) (hds_succ : ∀ (n : ℕ) (j : Fin (n + 1)), s n j ≫ d n j.succ = 𝟙 (U n)) (hds_gt : ∀ (n : ℕ) (i : Fin (n + 2)) (j : Fin (n + 1)), j.castSucc < i → s (n + 1) j.castSucc ≫ d (n + 1) i.succ = d n i ≫ s n j) (hss : ∀ (n : ℕ) (i j : Fin (n + 1)), i ≤ j → s n j ≫ s (n + 1) i.castSucc = s n i ≫ s (n + 1) j.succ) : (∀ (a b : Paths FreeSimplexQuiver) (p q : a ⟶ b), Relation.EqvGen (@HomRel.CompClosure (Paths FreeSimplexQuiver) _ FreeSimplexQuiver.homRel a b) p q → simplexWordEvaluation U d s p = simplexWordEvaluation U d s q) ∧ ∃ E : SimplexCategoryGenRelᵒᵖ ⥤ D, ∃ h : ∀ a : SimplexCategoryGenRel, E.obj (op a) = U a.len, (∀ (n : ℕ) (i : Fin (n + 2)), eqToHom (h (SimplexCategoryGenRel.mk (n + 1))).symm ≫ E.map (SimplexCategoryGenRel.δ i).op ≫ eqToHom (h (SimplexCategoryGenRel.mk n)) = d n i) ∧ (∀ (n : ℕ) (i : Fin (n + 1)), eqToHom (h (SimplexCategoryGenRel.mk n)).symm ≫ E.map (SimplexCategoryGenRel.σ i).op ≫ eqToHom (h (SimplexCategoryGenRel.mk (n + 1))) = s n i) ∧ (∀ (a b : Paths FreeSimplexQuiver) (w : a ⟶ b), eqToHom (h ((Quotient.functor FreeSimplexQuiver.homRel).obj b)).symm ≫ E.map ((Quotient.functor FreeSimplexQuiver.homRel).map w).op ≫ eqToHom (h ((Quotient.functor FreeSimplexQuiver.homRel).obj a)) = simplexWordEvaluation U d s w) ∧ (∀ (a b c : SimplexCategoryGenRel) (p : a ⟶ b) (q : b ⟶ c), E.map (p ≫ q).op = E.map q.op ≫ E.map p.op) ∧ (∀ a : Paths FreeSimplexQuiver, simplexWordEvaluation U d s (𝟙 a) = 𝟙 (U a.len))
